newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Jan 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Jan 28.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Tuesday:

* President Clinton will soon ask Congress to give tax credits to businesses hiring welfare recipients. The plan would let employers take a credit equal to 50 percent of the first $10,000 paid to a long-term welfare recipient.
* Index funds, which try to mimic the performance of the stock market by holding all the shares of a particular market index, have grown in popularity as the stock market continues to climb.

* The future of Atlantic City's casino industry is in question as the New York State Legislature prepares to vote on an amendment that would increase competition by legalizing gambling in other areas.
* The New York City police commissioner moves to punish officers in a labor contract dispute who have reduced the number of tickets they write and cost the city several million dollars.
* Syrians question whether recent events are a sign that President Hafez al-Assad is trying to root out corruption in order to prepare the way for a successor.
* A movement to eradicate all house cats in Australia gains support in Parliament and from conservationists who say the cats have led to the extinction of 39 species of smaller creatures.
